pr_body:
Fixes #5310

Presigned URLs are widely supported because they allow for easy sharing of private objects with anyone, with the added convenience of an expiration time.

- GCP https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/signed-urls
- AWS https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/ShareObjectPreSignedURL.html
- Minio https://min.io/docs/minio/linux/reference/minio-mc/mc-share-download.html
- Cloudflare R2 https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/data-access/s3-api/presigned-urls/

Currently, httpfs is unable to read from presigned URLs because when it reads a file, it sends a HEAD request first. However, presigned URLs may not handle HEAD requests properly. When a HEAD request fails, we can send another RANGE request as a fallback. The purpose of the RANGE request is to get the Content-Range, so we just need to request a one-byte range. The RANGE request will return a 206 HTTP code if the presigned URLs responds successfully.

When a range request's response is successful (status code 206), it will typically include the `Content-Range` header. Instead of using the `Content-Length` header, we can use the value provided in the `Content-Range` header to determine the length of the requested file.

Content-Range Header  will look like this 
`Content-Range: bytes 0-1/67589`

67589 is the file length 

- MDN https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Range

## Test 

We can use `Minio/mc share download` to ensure that we don't inadvertently break this feature. This command can be used to generate presigned URLs for sharing private content stored in an S3-compatible service.

~~The`MinIO` server container is added to the 'duckdb_network' network, which means that other `mc` client containers on the same network can also read from the server.~~
pr_comments:
Thanks @Tishj and @samansmink, for reviewing the code. Your work on require-env in sqllogictest has been very helpful.

I made the following changes after code review

1. To improve the formatting of error messages, formatted strings have been used in `IOException`.
2. To optimize performance and avoid unnecessary memory copies, nullptr is now passed to `GetRangeRequest` instead of a dummy buffer.
3. To handle unexpected or invalid values in the Content-Range header, an `IOException` is now thrown.

## generate_presigned_url.sh
~~The first two lines of generate_presigned_url.sh include unittests for `s3_presigned_upload.test` and `s3_presigned_upload.test_slow`. This may seem a little tricky or confusing. However, it is simply used to upload data files to Minio.😅~~

It is only possible to generate a presigned URL after a file has been uploaded. Therefore, to better control the test flow, a presigned_url.yml file has been created. However, as I am not very familiar with Docker, I am not sure if it is possible to compose mc after files have been uploaded to the Minio server. If this is possible, then I would be happy to merge presigned_url.yml with minio_s3.yml.

Also, the failed Windows CI and Python CI  works on my fork 

https://github.com/douenergy/duckdb/actions/runs/4303413571
https://github.com/douenergy/duckdb/actions/runs/4303413566

By the way, this is also work for Cloudflare R2 presigned url
@djouallah

1. 
```
aws s3 presign --endpoint-url 'https://<your-cloudflare-accountid>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com'  s3://<your-R2-bucket>/<your-csv>.csv --expires-in 36000 --profile <your-profile-in-aws-credentials-profile>  --region auto
```

2. 
```
duckdb -c "SELECT * FROM 'step-1-output-R2-presigned-url' " 
```

more info [R2 aws-cli doc](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/examples/aws-cli/)

issue_context.title: '403 Forbidden' for AWS s3 presigned URL
issue_context.body:
Hi. I am creating an Amazon s3 presigned URL to a CSV file using their Javascript SDK. The URL downloads the file fine in a browser which confirms it's OK, but if I use it in the duck cli or via the npm package with:

`create view test as select * from read_csv_auto('...presigned url...');`

I get `403 (Forbidden)`.

You can also test this by locating a CSV file in s3 via the AWS admin console and creating the URL with 'Object actions' ->  'Share with a presigned URL'.
comments: Can you please include all the version information requested in the issue template?

Hi, sorry - it's:

OS: Ubuntu 20.04.5 LTS
DuckDB Version: 0.5.1
DuckDB Client: npm

Also tried duck db cli but that's actually 0.5.0.
Okay, can you please try with the latest master version instead? You can install it with `duckdb@next`

```
at default_connection (node_modules/duckdb/lib/duckdb.js:384:32)

```

This at the place in my javascript where I am issuing the:
```
INSTALL httpfs;
LOAD httpfs;
```

Requests ahead of creating the view.

If I pause the code slightly before running this it then proceeds to give me the same `403 (Forbidden)` error as before.

@chrisbrain it's not a new requirement sorry, but a workaround for a bug that needs to be fixed

I'm not sure if we've done any/much testing with presigned urls to be honest, I'll see if I have time to investigate this week

Ah I see - OK well I think I confirmed it's still happening on the latest pre release version.

FWIW Dropbox has a kind-of-similar feature where they let you generate a URL which is valid for a few hours and that appears to be working fine with duckdb.

Thanks and appreciate anything you can do!

@Mause I am suspecting now that this happens because in the background duck is making both HTTP HEAD and GET requests and the presigned URLs are only for GET.

If that's the case it's quite unfortunate as this seems it would have provided a neat way to connect duck views to s3 files disparate buckets with different credentials.

Not sure if this is worth any thought but perhaps duckdb could be put into a mode where it uses GET to simulate HEAD requests as I saw mentioned here:
https://stackoverflow.com/a/39663152

But it may have other implications.

I also bumped into this problem, I think it's failing on the HEAD request as you mention, the error I was getting was:

`Invalid Error: Unable to connect to URL "https://....`

and that looks to be thrown when a non 200 response is returned from the HEAD request: https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/master/extension/httpfs/httpfs.cpp#L490

It would have been easier to spot what was going wrong if the error message had have said:

`Invalid Error: Unable to make HEAD request to URL "https://...`

I'll just workaround this by downloading the files and then loading them locally.
